source: Dr. Thaveesak Sangudom, Dr. Theerawut Chutinanthakun, and Wirot Horasart, "Off-season Production Techniques for Pursat Orange (ក្រូចពោធិ៍សាត់ / kroch poursat) in Cambodia," in The Guideline of Climate Change Adaptation in Cambodia (pp. 130-153), Project on Promoting Climate Resilience in Farming Communities of Cambodia, General Department of Agriculture (GDA) Cambodia, Thailand International Cooperation Agency (TICA), and Department of Agriculture (DOA) Thailand, 2017-2020.
text: After the harvest and the post-harvest pruning, trees are given a recovery fertilizer application (documented as Stage 1 / application 1 of the annual cycle, timed to November): organic fertilizer/compost at 5-10 kg per tree, plus NPK 15-15-15 chemical fertilizer at 0.5-2 kg per tree. The chemical fertilizer amount is adjusted according to the trunk diameter of each tree -- larger, more established trees receive more. This application is intended to fuel the new leaf flush and vegetative growth that follows pruning and the water-stress flowering trigger, and is followed by regular irrigation monitoring through December and January.
